analysis.title: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics Export Restrictions. Retail Sales/NVDA. Bonds vs Bond Proxies
key_insights: Asia is under pressure again. The market is digesting Jensen Huang's departure and the prospect of tighter US AI export controls (the MATCH Act and RASA). Lost chip export revenue could redirect supply into the US domestic market, while economies that depend on US technology face weaker near-term capex and possibly slower long-term productivity growth. Asia's supply chain is the most exposed.

Defensive equities have rallied by an extraordinary amount. Relative multiple expansion in defensives is approaching levels last seen decades ago. XLU has outperformed TLT by roughly 5 percentage points over the last 20 sessions, about 3 standard deviations on a 20-day basis.

The author asks what defensive stocks are pricing if bonds are not going to rally. With real and nominal yields where they are, the persistence of the rerating is surprising. Equities are pricing a growth scare that the bond market has not acknowledged.

Bonds did not rally on the prior session even though oil, stocks and growth expectations all fell, and the back end stayed subdued. Williams reiterated a cautious, hawkish-leaning stance and said policy must stay restrictive enough to bring inflation back to 2%.

Warsh spoke on the prior session and gave a more balanced view of AI, acknowledging the potential for an investment bust alongside the productivity upside. The author notes Warsh has a long record of focusing on financial conditions, particularly during the GFC. If equities keep falling, the distribution of rate outcomes should shift quickly away from hikes.

Recent IT disruptions at cloud infrastructure, commercial airlines and banks have not been confirmed as malicious cyber events. The author reads them as evidence of operational fragility in complex enterprise stacks and expects cybersecurity budgets to behave like non-discretionary capex. Spending is tilting toward automated threat detection, real-time telemetry and identity verification, and the author expects the extra spending to be baked in for 2027-30.

The author argues robotics is the larger AI unlock in the physical world while investors discard semiconductor exposure and 2028/2030 forecasts. GPU-accelerated simulation (NVIDIA Isaac Lab) and differentiable world models (SuperMimic compressed 100,000+ whole body motions into three hours on one GPU) have commoditized lower-level balance and locomotion training.

Retail sales are the main macro event of the session, alongside industrial production and more Fed speakers. Nvidia reports after the close. The author suspects near-term numbers could be robust, but the market has no agreed multiple for 2028, 2029 or 2030 earnings.
Equities are pricing a growth slowdown while rates and FX barely respond. Either equities are overreacting or rates and FX are underreacting. The recent NDX lows are the technical line in the sand.

tension_points.bull_case: Rates and FX are right that no growth scare is coming, so equities are overreacting and a base can form if the recent NDX lows hold.
tension_points.bear_case: Equities are correctly pricing a growth slowdown that rates and FX are underreacting to. Defensives trade at record relative multiples while bonds have not rallied.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the recent NDX lows would invalidate the base-forming case and risk another mechanical leg lower as CTAs sell.
